To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we propose to use a position-sensitive scorer to tackle the problem of incomplete answers, (2) we propose to build a hierarchical attention network with recurrent connections to tackle the problem that long documents are hard to represent, (3) we propose a pipeline of two linguistic verifiers to tackle both challenges.

(1) we propose a position-sensitive context verifier for machine reading comprehension that rewrites the question by replacing the interrogative words with the predicted answer phrases; and (2) we propose a hierarchical attention network that connects the segments in a long passage in a recurrent manner for answerablility prediction and boundary determination.

we have designed two linguistic verifiers to tackle two challenges in machine reading comprehension and have combined them into a pipeline to achieve significantly better results than state-of-the-arts on three benchmark datasets.

two aspects: how to better evaluate the syntactic quality of the predicted answers, and how to utilize long passages to help answer extraction and answerablility classification.
two challenges: how a model should understand a question to predict the right answer and how a model should comprehend long passages to predict the answerability of a segment.
